samples.summary: `logout()` erases offline data unconditionally, but the only writer of the identity it erases under is now behind `PrivateRoute`'s new `offlineInPlay` gate — a stale `wafflebase-offline-user` mirror lets one account's sign-out destroy a *different* account's archives
samples.evidence:
`api/auth.ts:135` calls `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` with no gate. That function resolves whose data to erase via `offlineUserId()` (`lib/offline-erase.ts`), which falls back to the persisted `wafflebase-offline-user` mirror. The ONLY place that writes or clears that identity is `rememberOfflineUser`, called at exactly one site: `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:66` — and `OfflineRuntime` is mounted only when `PrivateRoute.tsx:58`'s `offlineInPlay` (`PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30`) is true.

The mirror is cleared only on a *successful* `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`. A session that ends any other way — the 401 arm at `api/auth.ts:256` passes `eraseLocalData: "none"` and therefore never reaches `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)`; a closed browser never reaches it at all — leaves the mirror naming the previous account. If the next signed-in account does not mount `OfflineRuntime` (the pin-rollback case `PrivateRoute.tsx:31-44` explicitly contemplates: `supportsClientKey()` false and *that* account has no stored consent), `rememberOfflineUser` never runs, and their logout drives `eraseOfflineData(store, previousAccount)` plus `forgetDeviceSecret(previousAccount)` — deleting the previous account's live entries **and archives**, which by this feature's own design are the only copy of work the server never took.

The same stale-mirror read reaches `purgeOfflineDocuments` at `api/documents.ts:164` and `:215`, and `isOfflineUser` at `api/workspaces.ts:159`, none of which are gated either. Fix belongs on the new code: either set the identity unconditionally for any signed-in user, or have the erase refuse a mirror it cannot attribute to the session that is ending.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` now issues two extra requests — including an unfiltered `GET /documents` — on every call, with none of the gating the rest of the feature has
samples.evidence:
`api/workspaces.ts:127` runs `const doomed = await documentIdsIn(id);` before the DELETE, unconditionally. `documentIdsIn` (workspaces.ts:~101) calls `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and then `fetchDocuments()` — the unfiltered `GET /documents` listing.

The only caller is `packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:182` (`mutationFn: () => deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)`), which pays this on every workspace deletion whether or not offline persistence is in play. Contrast `removeMember` at `workspaces.ts:159`, which correctly gates the same call behind `isOfflineUser(String(userId))`, and `PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30`, whose whole stated purpose is that a user who cannot even be offered the feature must not pay for it — the unfiltered `GET /documents` is named there as the cost to avoid. `deleteWorkspace` has no equivalent gate, so on the shipped pin (`@yorkie-js/react` `0.7.22`, below `MinClientKeyVersion`) it buys two network round-trips and an extra failure surface in front of a destructive action for a purge that is guaranteed to be a no-op.

samples.summary: `@/app/settings/page` is now both statically and dynamically imported, so the lazy `/settings` route stops code-splitting and the settings page is pulled into all seven `AppSidebar` shells
samples.evidence:
`components/settings-dialog.tsx:7` statically imports `SettingsContent` from `@/app/settings/page`. `settings-dialog.tsx` is imported by `components/nav-user.tsx:22`, which is rendered at `components/app-sidebar.tsx:149`. `AppSidebar` has seven mounts — `app/Layout.tsx:70` plus the six editor shells (`app/documents/document-detail.tsx:677`, `app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:190`, `app/slides/slides-detail.tsx:402` and `:788`, `app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:253`, `app/board/board-detail.tsx:153`, `app/files/file-shell.tsx:100`) — a count `src/hooks/nav-items-single-source.test.ts:4` already pins.

Meanwhile `App.tsx:171` still routes `/settings` to a `lazyWithRetry(() => import("@/app/settings/page"))` component. A module reached by both a static import and a dynamic one is inlined into the static chunk by Rollup, so the lazy boundary is defeated: the settings page and its transitive imports now load with every editor rather than on demand. Functionally harmless; the `lazyWithRetry` wrapper at the route is now dead weight and the split is silently gone.

samples.summary: The second consumer of `SyncStatus.state` was not updated for the new `'saved-locally'` member or the new `null`, and now enumerates an incomplete union by hand
samples.evidence:
`components/sync-status/use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24` reads `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'not-saved' || state === 'saving';`. The diff widened `SyncStatus.state` to `SyncState | null` (`use-sync-status.ts:42`) and added `'saved-locally'` to `SyncState` (`sync-state.ts:20`), and updated `SyncStatusChip` for both — `sync-status-chip.tsx:151` and `:167` introduce `savedLocally` and `leavingLosesWork` — but this file, the only other consumer, was left alone.

It still works: this probe feeds `canReload` in `lib/lazy-with-retry.ts:158`/`:233`, whose action is `window.location.reload()` (`lazy-with-retry.ts:102`), a same-URL reload that the chip's own reasoning (`sync-status-chip.tsx:139-146`) says is safe for a durable document. So the omission is accidentally correct. But nothing in the file records that decision, the two files now disagree about what counts as at-risk, and the next change to either — e.g. making recovery navigate rather than reload — will silently discard a durable document's queue. Same for `state === null`, which lands on "nothing at risk" by falling off the end of the comparison rather than by any stated choice.

samples.summary: The new failed-open branch depends on `useDocument()` exposing `error`, which nothing in the repo confirms the pinned `@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22 actually returns
samples.evidence:
`use-sync-status.ts:78` now destructures `error` from `useDocument()`, and the whole new `state: null` behaviour (`use-sync-status.ts:~226-236`, and `sync-status-chip.tsx`'s `if (state === null) return null`) hangs off it. `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22` and `:99` pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` at `0.7.22` — the same version `lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts` treats as too old to carry a client key.

Every test that exercises this path supplies `error` from a hand-written mock (`tests/components/sync-status/use-sync-status.test.ts:9-16`, `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:14-20`), so the suite proves nothing about the real provider's shape. `packages/frontend` has no `tsc` lane, so an absent field would not be a type error either — `error` would simply be `undefined` forever, the branch would never fire, and the chip would go on showing `✓ Saved` over a document that failed to attach, which is exactly the bug the branch was added to fix. Worth confirming against the installed package before merge; if 0.7.22 does not surface it, the `@yorkie-js/react` pin needs bumping alongside this.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `logout()` at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:134-136 calls `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` with no identity gate; that function (lib/offline-erase.ts:310-347) resolves the victim via `offlineUserId()` (:98-107), which falls back to the persisted `wafflebase-offline-user` mirror (:62) and then erases live entries AND archives plus the device secret (`eraseOfflineData`, :27-40, no `keepArchives`). A repo-wide grep confirms the only production writer/clearer of that mirror is `rememberOfflineUser`, called at exactly one site: components/offline-runtime.tsx:66 — and `OfflineRuntime` mounts only behind `offlineInPlay` (PrivateRoute.tsx:58, defined :28-30 as `supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled(me.id)`, per-account per offline-persistence-preference.ts:103-110). The mirror is cleared only on a successful erase (offline-erase.ts:337); the 401 arm passes `eraseLocalData: "none"` (api/auth.ts:277) and so never clears it, and a closed browser never reaches it — leaving a stale mirror naming a previous account. Reachability is concrete rather than theoretical: package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react at 0.7.22, below MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82), so `supportsClientKey()` is false and `offlineInPlay` depends solely on the current account's consent — the pin-rollback case PrivateRoute.tsx:45-57 explicitly contemplates. A signed-in account without consent never runs `rememberOfflineUser`, and its logout drives `eraseOfflineData(store, previousAccount)` + `forgetDeviceSecret(previousAccount)`, destroying another account's archives. The same ungated read reaches `purgeOfflineDocuments` from api/documents.ts:167 and :215 and `isOfflineUser` at api/workspaces.ts:159. This is in-lane for blast radius: a gate added in the diff breaks an invariant that unchanged consumers outside the diff rely on. No guard exists anywhere that re-attributes or clears the mirror for a session that did not mount OfflineRuntime, so no refutation ground applies.
